issue_context.title: Source generator doesn't support [JsonExtensionData]

review_comments: It might make sense to stick a comment on this property explaining what it is and what it is used for. At first read, I don't really understand what a `RuntimeTypeRef` is.
I'm assuming this would not be used if the extension data property is of type `JsonObject`, right?
Why can't the FastPath support this?

Extension data properties (dictionaries) can have `typeof(object)` values which is a polymorphic scenario currently not supported in fast-path. Also, the ext. properties can be `JsonObject` - I spent some time prototyping support for this but the PR started getting too complex and large.

We always had `JsonExtensionData` as "not supported in fast path for 6.0" - https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/51945#issuecomment-827795787. Would have been nice to get it in now, but I don't think it's worth the extra complexity at this stage.
Do you think it makes sense to log this as an issue, explaining the limitations and concerns? At least then it will be written down somewhere.
Is this supposed to be part of this change? It seems unrelated...

Per https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/58912#discussion_r705797719, `JsonObject` can be used as ext. data. We need this to support that scenario (also for upcoming support for S.T.Json.Nodes types - https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/45448#issuecomment-915449217).
I must be missing something, but I'm not seeing where the generated code calls this. Can you point me to where it is used?

The code that calls it is generated implicitly on this line: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/f4afd921e20fc7e2d7f17543784e8d453f5bf57e/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/gen/JsonSourceGenerator.Emitter.cs#L292

`{typeFriendlyName}Converter` resolves to `JsonObjectConverter`.

Nit: what is this test meant to be testing? If it's ensuring that the serialization infrastructure can cope with many serialization in parallel, that is generally handled by xunit's capacity to run multiple tests in parallel. If it's testing something else, it should be refelected in the test name.

Yeah it's meant to ensure the serializer can cope with multiple serialization routines in parallel. In my experience it has caught a few issues in product changes, so I think it's beneficial to keep them. cc @steveharter
